text: The L and L Building is a historic two-story structure located in Billings, Montana, designed in the Italianate style and constructed between 1893 and 1896 by Sam and Yee Quong Lee, two brothers born in China who emigrated to the United States in 1865. The building originally served as a dry goods store, a restaurant, and a lodging house until the late 1910s, when the first floor was remodeled into a saloon and a liquor store. It later housed the Arcade Bar, which was described as "an eyesore and a gathering spot for the city's criminal underbelly." The bar was temporarily closed following a police raid in January 1993, during which a bartender and two customers were arrested on marijuana charges, and it ultimately closed in May 1994. The building underwent refurbishment from 2004 to 2006. It has been listed on the National Register of Historic Places since December 19, 2008.
